title: Australia Tightens Student Visa Rules: Five Changes Indian Students Must Know
excerpt: Most onshore applications closed on 2 October 2026, repeat student visas now need an exemption, partners and children can rarely be included and can never join later — and provider transfers are restricted for 12 months until June 2027.
body:
• From 2 October 2026, most temporary visa holders in Australia can no longer apply for a Student visa (subclass 500) onshore — they must lodge from outside Australia and be outside Australia when it is granted.
  • Current student visa holders can apply for another student visa in Australia only under one of six exemptions, including PhD study, DFAT or Defence sponsorship, and progression to a higher AQF-level course.
  • Most applicants can no longer include a partner or children unless an exemption applies, and family can never be added later as subsequent entrants — decide on family before you apply.
  • Applications lodged before 2 October 2026 are assessed under the old rules, and the provider-transfer restriction for non-school students is extended from 6 to 12 months until 30 June 2027.

Australia has tightened its student visa rules in the biggest overhaul of the subclass 500 program in years, and Indian students — one of the largest international cohorts — need to plan around five changes before they enrol, pay fees or book travel. The core package took effect on 2 October 2026, with a further biometric step reported from 26 October 2026, Education Times reported.

The Australian Department of Home Affairs states the position directly on its official changes page: from 2 October 2026 there are new rules for Student visa (subclass 500) and Student Guardian (subclass 590) visas, changing who can apply for and be granted a visa while in Australia and whether family members can be included. Australia continues to welcome international students, Home Affairs says, and students applying from India in the normal way are not banned — the restrictions bite mainly on people already in Australia, on repeat applications, and on family plans.

The five changes

1. Most onshore applications are closed. Holders of visas including Working Holiday (417 and 462), Training (407), Temporary Activity (408), Short Stay Specialist (400) and Skills in Demand (482) can no longer switch to a student visa from inside Australia. They must lodge from outside Australia and be outside Australia at grant, and they receive no Bridging Visa A for that application. An application lodged onshore by someone required to apply offshore can be invalid, with no right of review at the Administrative Review Tribunal, migration agents AUSCAN warn in their guide to the October 2026 rules.

https://x.com/EconomicTimes/status/2115045898862330025

2. A second student visa onshore needs an exemption. Current student visa holders can apply again in Australia only if they fit one of six exemptions: needing up to 12 more months to finish their main course with the same provider; DFAT or Defence sponsorship; applying for a PhD; applying for primary or secondary school; progressing to a higher AQF-level course after completing their main course; or being unable to continue because their provider defaulted.

3. Family inclusion is now the exception. Most applicants cannot include a partner or dependent children. For Indian applicants, the practical exemptions are PhD study, DFAT or Defence sponsorship, or a fully funded foreign government scholarship. Any family included must apply with the student, from the same location, at the same time.

4. Family cannot join later. Adding family members as subsequent entrants after the visa is granted is no longer possible, and there are no exemptions to this rule. Families must make the decision before the first application is lodged.

5. Changing provider got slower, and biometrics may be requested. From 2 October 2026 the restricted period before a non-school student can transfer education providers is temporarily extended from 6 months to 12 months, until 30 June 2027, Education Times reported, citing Unstop founder and CEO Ankit Aggarwal. Separately, from 26 October 2026, biometric information such as fingerprints and a facial image could be requested when a new Indian student visa application is lodged, and applicants must follow the instructions issued by the immigration authorities.

What Indian applicants should do now

The preparation advice in Education Times is practical: keep academic and financial documents ready, budget for the full cost of study — tuition, accommodation, food, transport, health insurance, travel and emergency savings — rather than relying on part-time work, and check accommodation before paying, including for online rental scams aimed at families arranging housing from India. Aggarwal's point, as reported, is that choosing a university is only one part of the decision; total cost, course suitability and career prospects after graduation decide whether the investment works.

Before lodging anything, applicants should read the Home Affairs changes page and the subclass 500 requirements for their own circumstances, because the same change affects students differently depending on their visa, course, provider and family situation. Home Affairs has also flagged further stages, including limits on Temporary Graduate (subclass 485) applicants including family members and a new transfer stream for students changing providers, with details not yet released.

items.text: 2 Oct 2026: most temporary visa holders (Working Holiday, Training, Skills in Demand and others) must apply for a student visa from outside Australia — and be outside Australia at grant
Second student visa onshore only with an exemption: same-provider course completion (up to 12 extra months), DFAT/Defence sponsorship, PhD, school studies, higher-AQF progression, or provider default
Partner/children can be included only if an exemption applies (e.g. PhD, DFAT/Defence sponsorship, fully funded foreign government scholarship) — and only at the time of applying
Family cannot be added later as subsequent entrants — no exemptions
Provider-transfer restriction extended from 6 to 12 months for non-school students until 30 June 2027
Applications lodged before 2 Oct 2026 are assessed under the old rules
From 26 Oct 2026, biometrics (fingerprints, facial image) may be requested for new Indian student visa applications
